name: Baikal-GVD

facility_roles.quote: constructed to study high-energy muon and neutrino fluxes and search for new types of elementary particles

intervals.label: first cluster deployed
intervals.quote: the first cluster of the Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) was deployed in early April, named "Dubna," comprising 192 optical modules
intervals.note: Named 'Dubna'; the status paper independently confirms the first cluster's deployment year as 2016 (see next interval), so 2015-2016 is recorded as the transition; the earlier 2015 date is the press account's.

intervals.label: expanding cluster array (ongoing)
intervals.quote: The first cluster of the Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope was deployed in 2016 with 288 OMs. Since then, there has been an annual increase of the deployed clusters.
intervals.note: As of the winter 2023 campaign: 3456 OMs on 96 strings (per the same source). Status remains 'construction' because the array is explicitly still being expanded toward its planned cubic-kilometre scale; not recorded as 'active' for the full design array.

summary.plain: A growing underwater telescope in Lake Baikal, Siberia, that has been adding new clusters of light sensors every year since 2016 in search of neutrinos from deep space.
summary.technical: Expanding underwater Cherenkov neutrino telescope in Lake Baikal's southern basin; first Baikal-GVD cluster deployed 2016, growing to 3456 OMs on 96 strings by the winter 2023 deployment campaign; still under active annual construction toward a design cubic-kilometre-scale volume.
